extracted.intended_audience: Prospective ARPA-E OPEN 2021 applicants (PIs, lead organizations, project teams preparing concept papers and full applications)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing and submitting Concept Papers and Full Applications to the ARPA-E OPEN 2021 (DE-FOA-0002459) funding opportunity, including eligibility, cost share, budget, team composition, IP/manufacturing obligations, and required templates/forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic manufacturing requirement for Subject Inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject Inventions – and related patents – arising from ARPA-E research projects must be manufactured/used for manufacture in the US (including U.S. territories) for sales anywhere in the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selected Applicants/Awardees may request “partial waivers” (modifications) of this requirement; such waivers are requested in the applicant’s Business Assurances Form (during Full Applications Phase of the FOA) and are negotiated with applicants selected for awards. ARPA-E has granted limited waivers for economic reasons with offsetting benefits to the US economy. Obligations applicable to subject inventions continue after the project is completed. See FAQ 119.3 and FOA Sec. VIII.A. Title to Subject Inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work must be conducted in the United States unless waived
rubrics_metrics.description: All work must be conducted in the US unless a partial waiver is granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: What constitutes 'work' may require clarification; foreign consultative activities (e.g., a third-party consultant based overseas giving verbal input with no funds or materials leaving the US) are addressed in FOA Section III and General FAQ 3.1. Waiver requests are handled via the Business Assurances Form in Full Application phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for small businesses/universities/non-profits and related manufacturing exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Small businesses, universities, and non-profits may apply, but there are exceptions for enhanced US manufacturing requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to FAQ 119.3 and FOA Section III for details about reduced cost share and any additional requirements linked to entity type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost sharing may be considered in selections
rubrics_metrics.description: ARPA‑E may consider the amount of cost share proposed when selecting applications for award negotiations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While reduced cost share eligibility exists (e.g., for small businesses), applicants should be aware cost share above the required minimum is a selection factor (see FOA p. 17 and p. 31 and FOA Sec. III.B.). Cost share may therefore impact competitiveness in final selections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single project-wide cost share percentage based on prime recipient
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost Share is calculated as a percentage of the Total Project Cost; ARPA‑E applies one cost sharing percentage to the project team as a whole, based on the prime recipient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Total Project Cost = prime recipient share + Federal share of total allowable costs. Consult FOA Sec. III.B. for specifics and General FAQ references (e.g., 4.5, 4.9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable costs follow FOA Funding Restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowable costs are defined under the FOA (see Section G. Funding Restrictions 1. Allowable Costs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must follow the FOA’s Allowable Costs section and any Budget Justification/SF‑424A Workbook guidance posted to ARPA‑E eXCHANGE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal pre-award and award content requirements (2 CFR applicability)
rubrics_metrics.description: 2 CFR Subpart C - Pre-Federal Award Requirements and Contents of Federal Awards applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indirect cost and other federal award requirements must comply with applicable 2 CFR provisions (see related FAQ references).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect cost rate limits must comply with 2 CFR 200.414
rubrics_metrics.description: All indirect cost (IDC) rate limits must be in accordance with 2 CFR Part 200.414.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should ensure IDC rates and documentation follow federal regulations and FOA instructions; see General FAQs 7.25 and 10.23 for related guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project team and application content can be modified in Full Application phase
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may expand or otherwise modify the Project Team (including technical points of contact), PI/co‑PI roles, title, abstract, budget, and other submission content in the Full Application phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ARPA‑E eXCHANGE system allows these edits during Full Application. See FOA Sec. IV.D. 'Content and Form of Full Applications' and related FAQs (e.g., Q136, Q137).

rubrics_metrics.name: Concept Paper submission required and FOA-specific
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must submit a Concept Paper in ARPA‑E eXCHANGE by the submission deadline to be eligible to submit a Full Application for a given FOA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concept Papers are FOA-specific and cannot be transferred between different FOAs. Applicants should not expect ARPA‑E to pre-assess which FOA is best; they must independently determine which FOA to respond to.

rubrics_metrics.name: ARPA‑E will not provide individualized Concept Paper feedback or disclose submission counts
rubrics_metrics.description: ARPA‑E does not provide specific comments/feedback on individual Concept Papers due to high volume and will not disclose the number of submitted Concept Papers or how many were encouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification letters will not include reviewer comments; historically typically one‑third to one‑half of applicants are encouraged to submit Full Applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget limits and award size range
rubrics_metrics.description: ARPA‑E may issue one, multiple, or no awards under the FOA; awards may vary between $250,000 and $10 million.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should propose within these limits and consult FOA Sec. II.A. 'Award Overview.' The total FOA budget may change via FOA modifications; applicants may edit requested funding in the Full Application phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include technical and financial details for all program phases
rubrics_metrics.description: For multi‑phase (e.g., 2‑phase) programs, the proposal package must include technical and financial details for each phase (both Phase 1 and Phase 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prime Recipients must complete each tab of the Budget Justification Workbook for the project as a whole, including work by prime, subrecipients, and contractors. See OPEN 2021 Technical Volume template and FOA Sec. IV.D.3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget period formatting and milestone consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget periods must be consistent with what is requested in the FOA (for OPEN 2021: 12 mo / 12 mo / 12 mo).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Go/no‑go milestones and budget periods must align with FOA requirements; applicants cannot arbitrarily set different period structures unless allowed by the FOA and Workbook Guidance (see General FAQ 10.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: TT&O (Technology Transfer & Outreach) activities are optional
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Teams may, if desired, include Federal funding for Technology Transfer & Outreach (TT&O) activities, but TT&O is not required for a proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although some Budget Workbook text previously indicated a 5% TT&O requirement, OPEN 2021 clarifies TT&O is optional and the Budget Workbook will be modified for consistency. Applicants may choose to include TT&O funds; ARPA‑E is required to allocate a percentage of appropriated funds to TT&O overall.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent prosecution and Subject Invention disclosure reimbursement cap
rubrics_metrics.description: ARPA‑E will reimburse the Prime Recipient up to $30,000 of expenditures for filing and prosecution of United States patent applications and allowable costs associated with Subject Invention disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The $30,000 cap is total for all recipients on a project; budget accordingly and consult General FAQ 7.18.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign travel is generally disallowed without prior approval
rubrics_metrics.description: ARPA‑E generally does not fund projects that involve foreign travel; recipients must obtain written authorization from the ARPA‑E Program Director before incurring any foreign travel costs and must provide trip reports with reimbursement requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restriction applies to travel to Canada and other foreign countries. Applicants may include foreign travel in their proposed budget but ARPA‑E reserves the right to approve or deny the travel.

rubrics_metrics.name: File format and submission format requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific file formats are required for submission elements (e.g., Summary Slide must be PowerPoint).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use non‑permitted formats such as Publisher for the Summary Slide; follow FOA Sec. IV.D and template instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal Qualification Summaries (PQS) length constraint
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Personal Qualification Summary (PQS) is limited to 3 pages in length; there is no cumulative page limit for PQSs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are no current prescribed content requirements for PQSs beyond the page limit; applicants may choose the content. FOA may be updated in future to provide more instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software Commercialization Plan required only for software/data projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are required to submit a Software Commercialization Plan only if a proposed project's primary outputs/results are expected to be software or data sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the project does not involve software as a primary output, a software commercialization plan is not required; provide commercialization content appropriate to the technology type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subrecipient Budget Justification threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Subrecipients that will perform 10% or more of the work (measured by Total Project Cost) must complete the Budget Justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FFRDCs and other organizations performing ≥10% of the work must complete the Budget Justification workbook; see General FAQ 7.10 and FOA guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fringe benefit form limitations and allowed addendum
rubrics_metrics.description: If the SF‑424A workbook structure does not match an applicant's fringe benefit accounting method (e.g., no negotiated flat rates), applicants may not request form modifications but may submit an addendum explaining how fringe benefits are calculated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ARPA‑E will not unlock locked workbook tabs; provide an addendum consistent with General FAQ 10.1 instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple submissions and funding of distinct concepts
rubrics_metrics.description: A team may submit more than one Concept Paper/proposal provided the submissions are scientifically distinct; more than one proposal from the same team may be funded if they are scientifically distinct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure distinctness is clear to avoid overlapping submissions; see FOA rules on scientific distinctness.

rubrics_metrics.name: ARPA‑E will not pre‑assess proposals or provide teaming guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: ARPA‑E will not pre-assess an applicant’s proposal or provide guidance on which FOA to target or on teaming arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective applicants must independently review technical requirements of FOAs and determine applicability and team arrangements; do not rely on ARPA‑E to advise selection between similar FOAs.
